decision: chose to make the auth question a design decision with an ADR, not code
why: the open question changes the protocol, and every app in every language would follow it

decision: set the rigor high for connector auth and low for platform-level auth
why: the manifest credential shape is hard to undo once apps depend on it, while platform login can be bought from an identity provider later

decision: asked three models for independent designs: Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1-sol and Grok 4.7
why: comparing designs from different model families catches blind spots that one model would miss

decision: all three designs agree: the OAuth flow runs in the platform, and platform logins never enter the protocol
why: the three models converged on this without seeing each other's work

decision: the designs split on where provider URLs live: candidates 1 and 3 put them in the app manifest with an operator pin, candidate 2 has the operator type them in

decision: recompiled all three sketches and mutation-tested candidate 1's type checks
why: a candidate's own claim that its sketch compiles is not proof

decision: picked candidate 1 as the base and overruled the judge, who picked candidate 2
why: candidate 2 moves provider URLs out of the app, which is the coupling Simon questioned. The judge's blockers against candidate 1 could be fixed with grafts

decision: grafted consent bound to the browser session, immutable OAuth bindings and a session sign-in from candidate 2
why: they fix judge findings F4 and F5

decision: kept protocol 1 and allowed breaking changes until the first external app ships
why: judge F6 flagged that required oauth2 endpoints break the schema, and no app depends on it yet

decision: wrote ADR 0011 for platform access and ADR 0012 for connector OAuth, both as Proposed

decision: a GPT-6.1-sol review of the merged design found round-1 issues F4 to F8 fixed and two new blockers, F12 and F13

decision: gave each OAuth binding its own redirect URI, checked against the pending connect

decision: made the delete on invalid_grant conditional on the stored record being unchanged
why: F13: a slow failed refresh could delete a fresh reconnect

decision: noted that endpoints are checked at runtime and that the binding id comes from the pending connect
why: F14 and F15 were non-blocking notes

decision: round-3 GPT review found F12 to F15 fixed and no new blockers
